resistor_resistance_and_thermal.125C_screen_note: Uses the datasheet ±400ppm/°C across its room-temperature/125°C test span. The resistor element temperature under braking is not predicted.
resistor_resistance_and_thermal.thermal_management_policy: Keep commanded average resistor power at or below 400W under the specified 0–60°C ambient and mounting conditions. Do not interrupt the sole braking resistor because a temperature sensor trips during braking; no fuse or BMS interlock is included.

reference_braking_for_comparison_only.normal_400W_limited_control_law: P(t)=min(400W, m*a_ref*v(t)); all brake energy is dissipated in the resistor
reference_braking_for_comparison_only.interpretation: 400W cap reduces initial level-ground deceleration from 3.9624m/s² to the power-limited value; once speed falls to the crossover, the reference deceleration is restored. The 260.4J kinetic energy still all goes to the resistor.

slope_parameter_capability.interpretation: At slopes where m*g*v*sin(theta)>400W, the single outlet cannot hold 15km/h at steady descent under this average power ceiling. This is a parameter capability boundary, not an assumed slope demand or proven vehicle limit.

selection_conclusion_for_document.candidate: one Uni-Royal HEWR500W 1Ω ±5% terminal-type resistor, code HEWRA0J0100500
selection_conclusion_for_document.continuous_case: At 60°C the manufacturer derating curve gives about 430W continuous. Set the normal average resistor command to 400W, leaving 30W margin. Under all battery/supercapacitor absorption set to zero, the 30kg/15km/h translation-only energy is 260.4J; the 400W-capped power-law stop is about 1.076s and 2.285m in the paper model. This is near the 3.9624m/s² comparison reference (uncapped 1.052s/2.191m) while keeping the resistor's requested average heat under its 60°C continuous rating.
selection_conclusion_for_document.low_bus_case: At 22.5V, Rmax=1.092Ω in the 125°C TCR screen still permits about 464W full-on, above the 400W command; ideal low-BUS power margin is about 63.6W.
selection_conclusion_for_document.high_bus_PWM_case: At 42V the worst screened full-on pulse is about 1.93kW/46.1A, below the 6.25×500W test-power number of 3.125kW and below 2.5×RCWV=55.9V. The separate maximum-overload-voltage limit and any repetitive PWM envelope still need factory confirmation; 42V is not treated as continuous full-on.
selection_conclusion_for_document.temperature_policy: No thermal fuse, BMS interlock, or overtemperature cutoff may interrupt the only braking energy outlet; manage the 0–60°C installation and 400W operating envelope by resistor rating and thermal design.
selection_conclusion_for_document.purchase_status: Code/range/form factor are supported by the published factory coding and datasheet; inventory, lead time, price, exact maximum overload voltage, and mounting/thermal conditions are not confirmed. Do not freeze purchase before quote and installation review.
